text: Szentes (Hungarian pronunciation: [ˈsɛntɛʃ]) is a town in south-eastern Hungary, located in Csongrád county near the Tisza river. It serves as a cultural and educational center in the region and is the third most populous town in Csongrád county, after Szeged and Hódmezővásárhely. The town is 82,6 km away from Kerekegyháza. The area has been inhabited since the Neolithic period, with the discovery of the Szegvár-tűzkövesi idol, one of the few Neolithic depictions of a male deity, found there. During the barbarian invasions, archaeological evidence shows hundreds of graves belonging to the Iazyges, Sarmatians, Gepids, Huns, and Avars, and certain accounts claim the legendary camp of Atilla the Hun was located at the confluence of the Tisza and Körös rivers. The town was first documented in a land-division in 1332 under the name "Scenthus" and was said to be inhabited by descendants of the Ond tribe, one of the seven tribes of Hungary, and also contained a stone church dedicated to Andrew the Apostle. Local tradition holds that Csongrad castle stood on the town's boundaries until the first Mongol invasion. After Hungary's defeat at the Battle of Mohács by Ottoman forces, taxes were imposed on Szentes by three different powers, prompting those who could leave to flee. The region endured severe hardship under Ottoman rule, with entire towns erased, and further losses occurred during the Long Turkish War, when many towns disappeared and Szentes' inhabitants sought refuge in nearby wetlands. In 1647, Ferdinand III was defeated by Ottoman forces outside Szentes, but the Ottoman forces withdrew from the region. In 1693, the area was scorched and pillaged by Crimean Tatars seeking food after their failed attempt to capture Gyula. In 1709, the town experienced a plague outbreak that killed over 1,000 inhabitants. The townspeople actively participated in the Hungarian Revolution of 1848, and Kossuth Lajos visited to recruit troops. Following the Habsburg suppression of the revolution, many young men were forcibly conscripted into the Imperial Army as punishment, and the mayor was sentenced to hard labour.
